paper_metadata.title: Achieving high strength-ductility synergy in dilute Mg-Al-Ca alloy by trace Ce addition

evidence.quote: In this work, the trace Ce atoms have been added into the low-alloyed Mg-Al-Ca matrix, and the microstructure and mechanical properties have been investigated. For the Mg-Al-Ca ternary alloy, the tensile yield strength (TYS) would be decreased from ~321 MPa at 260 °C (extrusion temperature) to ~294 MPa at 290 °C.
In contrast, the Mg-Al-Ca-Ce alloy can still exhibit the high YS of ~350 MPa and elongation of ~12.1% at higher extrusion temperature of 290 °C.

The billets Mg-1.2Al-0.4Ca wt% (termed as AX104) and Mg–1.2Al–0.4Ca–0.2Ce wt% (termed as AXE1040) were prepared by induction melting with commercial pure Mg (99.99 wt%), Al (99.99 wt%), Ca (99.99 wt%), and Mg-30 wt% Ce master alloy under a protective Ar atmosphere.

evidence.section: 3.1 Mechanical properties of as-extruded Mg samples
evidence.quote: The Mg-1.2Al-0.4Ca alloy extruded at 260 °C (sample designated as AX104-260) has a tensile YS of ~321 MPa, and elongation (EL) of ~9.6%.

evidence.section: 3.1 Mechanical properties of as-extruded Mg samples
evidence.quote: When the extrusion temperature is increased to ~290 °C (designated as AX104-290 sample), the EL is enhanced to ~11%, while the tensile YS is reduced to ~294 MPa, and the ultimate tensile strength (UTS) is decreased to ~314 MPa.

The billets Mg-1.2Al-0.4Ca wt% (termed as AX104) and Mg–1.2Al–0.4Ca–0.2Ce wt% (termed as AXE1040) were prepared by induction melting with commercial pure Mg (99.99 wt%), Al (99.99 wt%), Ca (99.99 wt%), and Mg-30 wt% Ce master alloy under a protective Ar atmosphere.

Importantly, high-density plate-like nano-phases with an average length of ~25 nm are observed along basal planes (Fig. 6f), which can be confirmed to be the Al2Ca phases, according to the EDS results in Fig. 6g.

According to the EDS results in Fig. 5c, d, the second-phase in the AXE1040-260 alloy should be Al2(Ca, Ce), since the second phases are enriched in high amount of Al (~28.98 at%), Ca (~8.29 at%) and Ce atoms (~5.47 at%), and some Ce atoms have dissolved into the Al2Ca matrix.

evidence.quote: A typical bimodal grain structure can be observed in AXE1040, which is also consistent with OM results in Fig. 2.

As a result, the typical fiber texture of <10–10>//ED with intensity of 8.87 multiple of random distribution (mrd.), can be observed due to the existence of un-DRXed regions, in Fig. 3a–c
Nevertheless, the typical fiber texture of <10–10>//ED can be still detected, and the intensity of texture can reach ~5.99 mrd., Fig. 3d–e.

In the un-DRXed regions, profuse residual dislocations (Fig. 8b) and ultra-fined subgrain lamellae with a width of 100–200 nm (Fig. 8d) are still remained after the higher temperature extrusion in AXE1040-290 alloy.
The planar segregations of Al, Ce and Ca atoms on the GBs are evidently detected, and concentrations are determined to be ~0.15 at%, ~0.25 at% and ~1.3 at%, respectively.
Meanwhile, a considerable number of residual dislocations, as shown by the red arrows, can be observed in the interior of the lamellar structure.

evidence.section: 4.1 The role of Ce addition in affecting DRX behavior
evidence.quote: In this sense, at a higher extrusion temperature in AXE1040-290 sample alloy, the movement of dislocations and GBs could be obviously retarded due to an enrichment of Al and Ce atoms along these defects.

Several fine DRXed grains can be also detected at the front of the LAGBs in Fig. 7d, indicating the activation of continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) process through the progressive rotation of sub-grains [23].
Formation of subgrain with strong texture, residual dislocations due to segregation and profuse nano-precipitations can together contribute to the high yield strength of Mg-Al-Ca-Ce alloy.

More importantly, the trace Ce atoms can promote the activation of non-basal dislocations in Mg matrix and also the weakened texture in DRXed grains. As a result, the ductility is also simultaneously improved by the trace addition of Ce atom into Mg-Al-Ca based alloy.
